title: Kahana vs Slack: Keep the Chat, Add the Shelf
excerpt: Slack is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. Kahana is the shelf and reading list beside the chat, not another inbox.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: ≈12M daily active users (DAUs) in workplace collaboration.
Used by teams and professional communities globally; part of Salesforce’s portfolio.
Free tier with severe limits; paid plans roughly USD 7–8.75 per user per month.

strengths.title: Professional-grade collaboration
strengths.detail: Channels, threads, DMs, search, and integrations, widely adopted for internal team communication.

strengths.title: Rich integrations
strengths.detail: 1,000+ integrations (Google Workspace, Office 365, project tools, CRMs) make it a workflow hub.

strengths.title: Polished UX for business users
strengths.detail: Designed for enterprises and startups; many professionals already know Slack.

strengths.title: Channel-based structure
strengths.detail: Clear organization by topic, team, or project, helpful for structured professional communities.

weaknesses.title: Free tier is very limited for communities
weaknesses.detail: Only ~90-day message history; older messages and limited integrations make it weak for serious communities.

weaknesses.title: Cost scales aggressively with members
weaknesses.detail: At ~USD 7.25–8.75/user/month, a 200-member community can cost USD 1,450+/month, often prohibitive.

weaknesses.title: Not designed for paid memberships
weaknesses.detail: No native membership tiers, payments, or gating, paid communities need external tools.

weaknesses.title: Limited branding and white-label
weaknesses.detail: Minimal branding control; workspace always looks like Slack aside from name and icon.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Slack is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Slack is a workplace software with channels that connect you to the people and information you work with every day.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Slack side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Slack you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Slack

You can use both. Slack keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Slack. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
